name: Prague
tagline: Central Europe's best-preserved historic capital, a hundred spires rising above the Vltava with a beer culture woven into everyday life.
highlight: Crossing Charles Bridge at first light, its baroque statues silhouetted against the castle before the day's crowds arrive.
shortDescription: Central Europe's best-preserved historic capital, home to Prague Castle, Charles Bridge and one of the world's great beer cultures.
metaDescription: A Prague travel guide: Prague Castle, Charles Bridge, the Astronomical Clock, Malá Strana, food and how to plan a visit to the Czech capital.
knownFor: Prague Castle, Charles Bridge, the Astronomical Clock

image.file: File:Czech-03993 - Boat Station & St. Vitus Cathedral (32980108646).jpg
image.alt: Prague's skyline along the Vltava River, with St Vitus Cathedral rising above Prague Castle

intro: Prague is genuinely one of Europe's most beautiful and best-preserved capitals, its medieval, gothic and baroque architecture largely untouched by the wars that devastated so many other cities on the continent.

Its layout genuinely rewards wandering on foot — Prague Castle looms above the Vltava, Charles Bridge connects the old town to the castle district, and the whole historic core fits within an easily walkable area.
It's also genuinely a city built for beer, with pubs on nearly every corner pouring some of the best, cheapest pilsner anywhere in the world.

whyVisit.intro: Prague's case rests genuinely on an intact historic core paired with a living, everyday beer and pub culture.

points.title: Prague's historic centre is genuinely astonishingly intact
points.text: Spared the wartime bombing that levelled so many other European capitals.

points.title: Prague Castle is genuinely the largest ancient castle complex in the world
points.text: A thousand-year-old seat of power still central to Czech political life today.

points.title: The beer culture here is genuinely unmatched
points.text: World-class, inexpensive pilsner served in pubs on almost every corner.

points.title: It's genuinely one of Europe's most walkable capitals
points.text: Old Town, Malá Strana and the castle district all connect easily on foot.

points.title: It works genuinely well as a springboard for Bohemia
points.text: Day trips to Kutná Hora and Český Krumlov are both easy from here.

attractionsIntro: Prague's essential sights are genuinely concentrated within an easily walkable historic core.

attractions.name: Prague Castle

image.file: File:Castillo de Praga, Praga, República Checa, 2022-07-02, DD 209.jpg
image.alt: Prague Castle overlooking the city

attractions.text: Genuinely the largest ancient castle complex in the world, a thousand-year-old seat of Czech power above the Vltava.
attractions.tip: Genuinely arrive right at opening to see the changing of the guard without the midday crowds.

attractions.name: Charles Bridge

image.file: File:North view of Charles Bridge from Mánesův most, Prague 20160808 1.jpg
image.alt: Charles Bridge crossing the Vltava River in Prague

attractions.text: Genuinely a 14th-century stone bridge lined with baroque statues, the city's most iconic crossing.
attractions.tip: Genuinely cross at sunrise for photos without the crowds and street vendors that fill it by mid-morning.

attractions.name: Old Town Square and the Astronomical Clock

image.alt: The Astronomical Clock on Old Town Square in Prague

attractions.text: Genuinely the city's medieval heart, a working 15th-century astronomical clock still drawing crowds every hour.
attractions.tip: Genuinely climb the Old Town Hall tower for a view over the square itself, rather than just the clock.

attractions.name: St Vitus Cathedral

image.file: File:Interior of St. Vitus Cathedral Prague 01.jpg
image.alt: The Gothic interior of St Vitus Cathedral in Prague

attractions.text: Genuinely a soaring Gothic cathedral within the castle complex, its stained glass and vaulted ceilings centuries in the making.
attractions.tip: Genuinely look for the Art Nouveau stained glass window by Alfons Mucha in the third chapel.

attractions.name: Malá Strana

image.file: File:20190817 View of Malá Strana from Petřín 1354 5556.jpg
image.alt: The Malá Strana district of Prague below the castle

attractions.text: Genuinely Prague's best-preserved baroque district, a maze of cobbled lanes, palace gardens and quiet squares below the castle.
attractions.tip: Genuinely get lost on purpose here — the quieter side streets are the district's real reward.

attractions.name: The Jewish Quarter (Josefov)

image.alt: Historic synagogue buildings in Prague's Josefov district

attractions.text: Genuinely one of Europe's best-preserved former Jewish quarters, its synagogues and old cemetery a moving, essential visit.
attractions.tip: Genuinely buy a combined ticket covering several synagogues and the Old Jewish Cemetery together.

attractions.name: Petřín Hill and Lookout Tower

image.alt: The Petřín Lookout Tower above Prague

attractions.text: Genuinely a green escape from the crowds, a hilltop park topped by a miniature Eiffel-style lookout tower.
attractions.tip: Genuinely ride the funicular up and walk back down through the orchards.

thingsToDoIntro: Prague genuinely rewards unhurried wandering, though a few essential experiences anchor most visits.

thingsToDo.title: Cross Charles Bridge at sunrise

image.alt: Charles Bridge at sunrise in Prague

thingsToDo.text: A genuinely essential Prague ritual, having the bridge's statues almost to yourself before the crowds arrive.
thingsToDo.tip: Genuinely bring a coffee to go and continue on toward the castle while the light is still soft.

thingsToDo.title: Tour Prague Castle's grounds

image.alt: Prague Castle at dusk

thingsToDo.text: A genuinely essential half-day, taking in St Vitus Cathedral, the Old Royal Palace and Golden Lane.
thingsToDo.tip: Genuinely buy your ticket online in advance to skip the entrance queue.

thingsToDo.title: Watch the Astronomical Clock strike the hour

image.alt: The face of Prague's Astronomical Clock

thingsToDo.text: A genuinely medieval spectacle, apostle figures processing past two small windows as the clock strikes.
thingsToDo.tip: Genuinely temper expectations — the show itself is brief, the clock's mechanism is the real marvel.

thingsToDo.title: Wander Malá Strana's palace gardens

image.file: File:Praha Mala Strana Mala Palffyovska zahrada zidka.jpg
image.alt: A terraced palace garden in Malá Strana, Prague

thingsToDo.text: A genuinely peaceful escape, a string of baroque terraced gardens climbing the hill below the castle.
thingsToDo.tip: Genuinely several gardens connect by internal stairways — a single ticket often covers more than one.

thingsToDo.title: Climb Petřín Hill for the view

image.file: File:20190817 View of Prague Castle from Petřín 1345 5542.jpg
image.alt: The view of Prague Castle from Petřín Hill

thingsToDo.text: A genuinely rewarding walk or funicular ride, with one of the city's best panoramic views from the top.
thingsToDo.tip: Genuinely visit at golden hour, when the light over the castle and river is at its best.

thingsToDo.title: Explore the Jewish Quarter's synagogues

image.alt: Exploring Prague's historic Jewish Quarter

thingsToDo.text: A genuinely moving, essential few hours, tracing centuries of Prague's Jewish history through its synagogues and cemetery.
thingsToDo.tip: Genuinely allow at least two to three hours to do the quarter justice.

foodIntro: Prague's food genuinely means hearty Czech classics best paired with a proper pilsner.

foods.name: Svíčková (marinated beef in cream sauce)

image.alt: Svíčková, marinated beef in cream sauce with bread dumplings

foods.text: Genuinely the dish most Czechs would call their national favourite, tender beef with cream sauce and dumplings.

foods.name: Guláš with dumplings

image.alt: Czech goulash served with bread dumplings

foods.text: Genuinely a pub staple, rich paprika-spiced beef stew mopped up with sliced bread dumplings.

foods.name: Vepřové koleno (roast pork knee)

image.file: File:Salad and Czech roast pork knee.jpg
image.alt: Roast pork knee, a hearty Czech pub dish

foods.text: Genuinely a hearty, shareable pub classic, slow-roasted pork knee with crackling skin and mustard.
foods.whereToTry: Traditional beer halls throughout the city.

foods.name: Trdelník (chimney cake)

image.alt: Trdelník, a rolled pastry cooked over an open flame

foods.text: Genuinely more a Prague street tradition than an old family recipe, a sugar-and-cinnamon pastry cooked on a spit.
foods.whereToTry: Street stalls throughout the Old Town and near Charles Bridge.

foods.name: Czech beer (pivo)

image.alt: A glass of Czech pilsner beer

foods.text: Genuinely essential, some of the best and cheapest beer anywhere, poured properly in pubs across the city.
foods.whereToTry: Pubs on nearly every street in the city centre.

foods.name: Smažený sýr (fried cheese)

image.file: File:Smažený sýr s tatarskou omáčkou a brambory.jpg
image.alt: Smažený sýr, breaded fried cheese with tartar sauce and potatoes

foods.text: Genuinely a beloved pub classic, breaded and deep-fried cheese served with tartar sauce and fries.

accommodation.intro: Prague genuinely offers accommodation for every budget, from hostels to grand historic hotels.

areas.name: Old Town and Josefov
areas.bestFor: Being genuinely central and within walking distance of every major sight
areas.text: The most convenient base, though also the busiest and priciest part of the city.

areas.name: Malá Strana and the castle district
areas.bestFor: A genuinely quieter, more atmospheric stay close to the castle
areas.text: Cobbled lanes and fewer crowds, still an easy walk across the river to Old Town.

budget.label: Half-litre of Czech beer
budget.value: About Kč50–90 in a proper pub

gettingThere.intro: Prague is genuinely well connected by air, rail and road to the rest of Europe.

options.mode: Flight into Václav Havel Airport Prague
options.text: Genuinely the standard way in for most international visitors.
options.detail: A direct bus or taxi reaches the city centre in about 30–45 minutes.

options.mode: Train from Vienna, Berlin or Budapest
options.text: Genuinely a comfortable, scenic overland option from several neighbouring capitals.
options.detail: Journey times range from about four to seven hours depending on the route.

options.text: Genuinely a budget-friendly option from across Central Europe.
options.detail: RegioJet and FlixBus both run frequent, comfortable international routes.

gettingAround.intro: Prague's genuinely excellent public transport makes a car entirely unnecessary.

options.text: Genuinely fast and frequent, covering the whole city on one unified ticket.
options.detail: Trams are often the more scenic way to cross the city centre.

options.text: Genuinely the best way to see the historic core itself.
options.detail: Old Town, Malá Strana and the castle district all connect easily on foot.

options.text: Genuinely useful late at night or for luggage.
options.detail: Use a rideshare app or a registered taxi rank rather than hailing on the street.

bestTime.headline: May, June and September for mild weather and manageable crowds
bestTime.summary: Prague is genuinely a year-round destination, though shoulder-season months offer the best overall balance.

seasons.text: Genuinely mild temperatures and blooming parks, before peak summer crowds arrive.
Genuinely warm and lively, though the Old Town and castle get genuinely crowded.
Genuinely golden light over the rooftops, with noticeably thinner crowds than summer.
Genuinely atmospheric around the December Christmas markets, though short days and cold call for warm layers.

bestTime.avoid: Nothing strongly — Prague genuinely works year-round, though August's crowds are worth planning around.

itinerary.title: Three days in Prague
itinerary.intro: Built around the castle district, the Old Town, and a slower day exploring Malá Strana and Josefov.

days.title: Old Town and Charles Bridge
days.morning: Old Town Square and the Astronomical Clock.
days.afternoon: Cross Charles Bridge into Malá Strana.
days.evening: Dinner near the river, with the castle lit up after dark.

days.title: Prague Castle
days.summary: A full day exploring the castle complex.
days.morning: Prague Castle's grounds and the changing of the guard.
days.afternoon: St Vitus Cathedral and the Old Royal Palace.
days.evening: A pub dinner in Malá Strana.

days.title: Josefov and Petřín Hill
days.summary: The Jewish Quarter and a hilltop view.
days.morning: The synagogues and cemetery of Josefov.
days.afternoon: The funicular up Petřín Hill for the view.
days.evening: A final dinner back in the Old Town.

tipsIntro: Practical notes that make a Prague visit noticeably smoother.
tips: Buy genuinely a multi-day public transport pass if you're staying more than a couple of days.
Book genuinely Prague Castle's interiors online ahead to skip the entrance queue.
Carry genuinely some cash for small pubs and markets, even though cards are widely accepted.
Avoid genuinely restaurants with staff actively calling people in near major squares — check prices first.
Validate genuinely any paper transport ticket before boarding — inspectors do check.
Cross genuinely Charles Bridge at sunrise or late evening to avoid the worst of the crowds.

faq.q: How many days do you need in Prague?
faq.a: Three to four days genuinely covers the essential sights at a comfortable pace, with time for a day trip.
Genuinely more affordable than Western European capitals overall, though prices in the most touristy central areas have risen close to Western levels.

faq.q: Is Prague Castle worth the visit?
faq.a: Yes, genuinely — it's the largest ancient castle complex in the world, and St Vitus Cathedral alone justifies the trip up the hill.

faq.q: Do you need to book Charles Bridge or Old Town Square ahead?
faq.a: No, genuinely not — they're open public spaces, though visiting early morning avoids the worst crowds.
Yes, genuinely one of Europe's most walkable capitals — Old Town, Malá Strana and the castle district all connect easily on foot.
Yes, genuinely easily — Kutná Hora and Český Krumlov are both popular, straightforward day trips by train or organised tour.
